THE HEADLINES:-

 

 

  1. Shiromani Akali Dal returns to NDA ahead of Punjab Assembly polls; Prime Minister Narendra Modi stresses alliance will ensure people-centric governance and accelerate Punjab’s development.

 

  1. Prime Minister Modi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz review progress in Strategic Partnership; Reaffirm commitment to boost cooperation in defence, technology, trade and investment.

 

  1. India’s space economy to reach 40 to 45 billion dollars in under a decade as private sector drives growth, says Union Minister Jitendra Singh.

 

  1. Celebrations of Guru Nanak Jayanti and Dev Deepawali on Kartik Purnima draw large number of devotees to gurudwaras and temples across the country.

 

  1. WAVES Film Bazaar concludes at IFFI in Goa, marking 20 years of connecting Indian cinema and with global industry.

 

  1. In Asia Cup Rising Stars Cricket tournament, India A beat UAE by seven wickets in group-stage match in Qatar; Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashes fastest century and double century in List A.

 

<><><> 

 

The Shiromani Akali Dal has rejoined the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. The Bharatiya Janata Party and the Shiromani Akali Dal will contest the upcoming polls together, with both parties expressing commitment to Punjab’s development and progress. The announcement was made by senior BJP leader and Home Minister Amit Shah at the party headquarters in New Delhi today.

 

Speaking to media, Shiromani Akali Dal President Sukhbir Singh Badal said, whenever the two parties have formed governments together, Punjab has witnessed progress, peace, stability and communal harmony.

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed happiness over the Shiromani Akali Dal rejoining the National Democratic Alliance. In a social media post, Mr Modi said, the alliance was a natural partnership that will ensure people-centric governance in Punjab and take the state to new heights of progress. He also expressed confidence that the alliance would emerge as the preferred choice of the people of Punjab.

 

<><><> 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz today reviewed the progress of their Strategic Partnership and expressed satisfaction over the continued momentum in bilateral engagements. Mr Modi received a telephone call from the German Chancellor today. As India and Germany mark 75 years of diplomatic relations this year, the two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation across key sectors, including defence, trade and investment, and advanced technologies. They noted that the India-EU Free Trade Agreement will open up new opportunities for expanding bilateral trade and investment. Mr Modi and Mr Merz agreed to continue working closely to promote global peace, stability and a rules-based international order.

 

<><><> 

 

Communications Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said, India has transformed from a consumer of technology into a creator of technology over the past decade. Mr Scindia was addressing the Telecom Startups and MSME Conclave 2026 in New Delhi today. The Minister said India now has more than two lakh startups, a growth driven by several initiatives undertaken the NDA government of the past decade. Highlighting the growth of digital connectivity, the Minister said India currently has around 110 crore internet connections and 104 crore broadband connections. He also emphasised that India is the only telecom market in the world witnessing double-digit growth.

 

<><><> 

 

Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said, India’s space economy, currently valued at nearly 9 billion US dollars, is projected to grow to 40 to 45 billion US dollars in less than a decade. The Minister was addressing the fifth India International Space Conclave 2026 in New Delhi today. Dr Singh said the establishment of NewSpace India Limited, followed by the creation of IN-SPACe and the opening up of the space sector to private participation, marked a major transformation in India’s space journey. Referring to the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, the Minister said space-based applications help improve infrastructure planning and ensure timely project completion.

 

<><><>

 

Celebrations of Guru Nanak Jayanti and Dev Deepawali on Kartik Purnima drew large numbers of devotees to gurdwaras and temples across the country today.

 

Guru Nanak Jayanti, also known as Gurpurab and Parkash Purab, is being celebrated across the country and around the world with great religious fervour and devotion. The occasion marks the 557th birth anniversary of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism.

 

Guru Nanak Dev Ji was born in 1469 on Kartik Purnima, the full moon day of the lunar month of Kartik. His teachings of oneness, equality, compassion and selfless service continue to inspire millions across the world.

 

Gurdwaras across the country, including the Golden Temple in Amritsar, have been beautifully decorated with lights and flowers to mark the auspicious occasion. In Delhi, devotees are thronging historic gurdwaras to offer prayers and participate in special kirtan programmes.

 

“Processions and prayers marked Gurpurab – the birth anniversary of  Guru Nanak Dev in Delhi. Lakhs of devotees thronged historic Gurdwaras in the national capital including Bangla Sahib, Sis Ganj, Rakab Ganj, Nanak Piao, Damdama Sahib and Gurudwara Bala Sahib since morning and offered prayers. Early morning processions, also known as prabhat pheris were taken out by gurdwaras across the city carrying flags and singing devotional songs. Akhand Path and free community langar were also organised to mark the occasion. On the eve of Guru Nanak Jayanti yesterday , Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended a Shabad Kirtan at Lok Niwas hosted by Delhi Lieutenant Governor. Today Vice President C P Radhakrishnan visited Gurudwara Rakab Ganj Sahib and offered prayers. ANUPAM MISHRA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

 

On the auspicious occasion of Kartik Purnima, people across the country took holy dips in rivers, while the holy city of Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh witnessed Dev Deepawali celeberations, also known as the Festival of Lights of the Gods, this evening. Our correspondent has the details:
 

“Tourism and Culture Minister of state Jaiveer Singh inaugurated the celebrations by lighting a ceremonial lamp at Namo Ghat. Around 11 lakh earthen lamps illuminated all 84 ghats of Kashi, while the traditional Ganga Aarti was performed on various ghats. Lakhs of devotees and tourists from across the country and abroad reached Varanasi to witness the grand celebrations. A spectacular 3D projection mapping and laser show a grand display featuring 2,100 indigenous drones was also organised. Dev Deepawali celebrations were also organised along the banks of the Mandakini River in Chitrakoot and at the banks of major rivers in several other cities across the state. SUSHIL CHANDRA TIWARI AAKASHWANI NEWS LUCKNOW .”

 

The President, Vice President and Prime Minister extended their greetings to the people on the occasion of Parkash Purab and Dev Deepawali.

 

<><><> 

 

President Droupadi Murmu has said, despite global uncertainties and financial instability, India’s steady progress reflects the country’s commitment towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat. The President was speaking after inaugurating the historic Bali Jatra festival at Cuttack in Odisha this evening. She said the festival is one of Asia’s largest open-air annual trade fairs and celebrates Odisha’s glorious ancient maritime heritage. The annual festival in Odisha begins on Kartik Purnima, celebrated today with the traditional Boita Bandana ritual, in which people set afloat miniature boats to commemorate the state’s glorious maritime heritage and its ancient trade links with Southeast Asian countries.

 

At the venue, the President opened the ‘Cuttack in Cuttack’ theme pavilion. This year’s Bali Jatra, will continue for eight days until 1st of December.

 

<><><> 

 

The International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today witnessed a diverse line-up of films and engaging masterclasses captivating film enthusiasts. The screenings and interactive sessions offered movie buffs an opportunity to explore different aspects of cinema and learn from industry experts. Meanwhile, five-day WAVES Film Bazaar, marking two decades of connecting Indian cinema with the global film industry, concluded at the festival today. It provided a platform for filmmakers, producers, writers, investors and distributors from India and abroad to exchange ideas, develop film projects and explore opportunities for international collaboration.

 

“Various film makers spoke about their films today. Mohammadreza Ardalan who is the Director of Iranian film ‘Poultry Farm’ told how his film explores vulnerability of undocumented children. Filmmaker Akhil Sathyan of movie Sarvam Maya said humour can draw audiences into a story and make its emotional moments more affecting. A restored version of Bhalji Pendharkar’s Marathi film Sadhi Manase was screened at the IFFI today. At the inaugural edition of Prasar Bharati’s Script Pitching Lab, ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’. Avishesh Jha won the first prize Satya Vyas secured the Silver Award, while Jitesh Thakur won the Bronze. The five-day WAVES Film Bazaar 2026 concluded today. Additional Secretary, Shri Prabhat highlighted global networking, co-production and  financing opportunities coming due to film bazaars. Mahesh Chopade Akashvani News Panaji.”

 

<><><> 

 

London School of Economics and Political Science, Delhi School of Economics and the Institute of Economic Growth signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in New Delhi in the presence of Vice President CP Radhakrishnan. Speaking at the event, the Vice President said, the agreement aims to strengthen academic collaboration and the sharing of knowledge.

 

<><><> 

 

Maldivian Foreign Minister Iruthisham Adam arrived in New Delhi today to participate in the 25th IORA Council of Ministers Meeting. The 25th Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) Meeting of the Council of Ministers will be held in New Delhi on Friday.

 

<><><> 

 

The European Union (EU) and the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) held their first-ever high-level roundtable on maritime security in New Delhi today. Representatives from countries across the Indian Ocean region discussed ways to strengthen maritime domain awareness, combat piracy and trafficking, and enhance cooperation to safeguard critical sea lanes. Addressing the gathering, EU Ambassador to India Jean-Eric Paquet said the European Union was ready to intensify cooperation and joint efforts with regional partners to tackle maritime crime in the Indian Ocean.

 

<><><> 

 

In Sports, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi created history by smashing the world record for the fastest century and double century in List A cricket as India ‘A’ defeated the United Arab Emirates by seven wickets in a group stage match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament at Doha in Qatar. Chasing a target of 250 runs set by the UAE, India ‘A’ comfortably reached the target in just 14.2 overs for the loss of three wickets. Vaibhav smashed 204 runs off just 53 balls, reaching his century in only 28 deliveries to register the fastest hundred in List A cricket.The young batting prodigy then went on to complete his double century in just 52 balls with 28 sixes and seven fours, setting another world record of the fastest double century.

 

<><><> 

 

In Hockey, India thrashed China 6-2 in their league-stage encounter of the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal. This was India’s fourth consecutive victory in the tournament. They have already secured their place in the semifinals.

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi says, India-Nepal relationship is rooted in a deep sense of belonging and unwavering trust.

 

  1. Prime Minister calls for collective efforts to keep the youth away from drugs; Says trap of addiction shatters dreams of entire family.

India and Nepal today adopted a joint vision laying roadmap for a future-oriented partnership between the two countries. New Delhi also announced development package worth 24,000 crore Nepali rupees for the Himalayan nation. Both the countries signed eight agreements for collaboration in different fields including Health, traditional medicine, establishment of satellite communication network and capacity building training programme among others. The agreements were signed after talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi. Both leaders held wide ranging discussions on bilateral, regional and global issues.

 

Later in joint press statement, Prime Minister Modi said, India-Nepal relations are woven together by shared history, faith, culture and deep people-to-people ties. He also announced the Joint vision adopted by the two nations.       

 

The Prime Minister highlighted that in keeping with the spirit of Neighbourhood First Policy, despite serious challenges related to oil supply this year, India maintained the supply of fuel, fertilizers and other essential goods to Nepal.

The Prime Minister said, young creators from India and Nepal should work together and take the shared heritage to the world through new platforms like Waves.

 

The Nepalese Prime Minister said in his statement that India is a trusted partner of Nepal and the trust stands as high as the Himalayas. Mr Shah called for expanding air connectivity between both countries.    

 

“Prime Minister Narendra Modi reaffirmed India’s unwavering support to Nepal’s development journey as a close friend and neighbour. The Joint Press Release on the State Visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal said that India will extend development assistance of 15,000 crore rupees comprising a grant assistance of 3,500 crore rupees for post-disaster reconstruction and new infrastructure projects in Nepal. It will also extend a Rupee-denominated Line of Credit of 11,500 crore rupees for energy sector projects. Specific projects as well as modalities for the provision of development assistance will be finalized through mutual consultations. Both leaders expressed satisfaction at the ongoing progress in the implementation of development projects in Nepal, including the High Impact Community Development Projects. Suparna Saikia, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

 

Both Prime Ministers jointly flagged  off the new weekly train service – Saryu Kamala Express between Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh and Janakpur Dham in Nepal through video conferencing from New Delhi.

 

The Nepalese Prime Minister also called on President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan. 

 

<><><> 

 

Briefing the media in New Delhi, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said Prime Minister Modi and Prime Minister Balendra Shah held a very productive set of discussions today.

 

<><><> 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the Sikh tradition has always symbolised the spirit of sacrificing everything for the nation and its culture. The Prime Minister said this while attending Shabad Kirtan at Lok Niwas, the residence of Lieutenant Governor of Delhi Taranjit Singh Sandhu in New Delhi. Quoting Guru Nanak Dev’s teachings, the Prime Minister said Guru Nanak Dev’s principles have been an integral part of his life.

 

Highlighting the challenge of drug abuse in society, the Prime Minister said that falling into the trap of addiction shattered the dreams of the entire family. Mr Modi called for collective efforts to ensure that every young person in the country remains free from drugs.

 

The Prime Minister said this year’s Prakash Parv holds special significance as it marks 350 years of the martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur.

 

<><><> 

 

President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people on the eve of Prakash Parv of Guru Nanak Dev ji. The President said, the message of ‘Ik Onkar’ given by Guru Nanak Dev is a message of the unity of all humanity. She highlighted that Guru Nanak Dev emphasised the need to build a society free from caste distinctions, social hierarchies and discrimination. He also taught that love, compassion and service to humanity should form the foundation of one’s life.

 

{<><><>}

 

Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has said that India has lifted 50 crore people out of extreme poverty through a whole-of-government approach. Citing a recent World Bank report recognising the rapid pace of poverty reduction in the country, Mr Chouhan said the agriculture sector is playing a significant role in this achievement. The Minister was addressing a workshop on the Role and Contribution of Agriculture in Reduction of Poverty in India in New Delhi today.

 

<><><>

 

The Home Ministry has advised WhatsApp users to exercise caution while using WhatsApp web. In an advisory, the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) said that its National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit has observed that an authenticated WhatsApp web session can be misused to gain unauthorised access to a user’s WhatsApp account.

 

“According to the advisory, such unauthorised access may allow malicious persons to read messages and send messages while impersonating the user. The advisory stated that it also allows access to contacts and group conversations and may be misused to exploit the trusted identity of the account holder for fraud, phishing, social engineering, and other malicious activities. The advisory suggested avoiding official or sensitive work, including exchange of official, organisational, financial, confidential, or other sensitive information via WhatsApp Web on computers. Users have also been advised not to keep WhatsApp Web permanently logged in and to manually log out after every session. It advised users to avoid logging in to WhatsApp Web through cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres, borrowed computers or other untrusted systems. Akshit Vaidyan, Akashvani News Delhi.”

 

<><><> 

 

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed additional preventive safeguards for electronic banking transactions (EBTs) to strengthen customer protection against digital payment frauds. The draft amendment directions seek to give customers greater control over the manner and extent of use of digital payment channels. The RBI has also proposed expanding the definition of ‘negligence by banks’ to ensure uniformity in banking practices and protect customers against omissions or commissions by banks.

                                                      

<><><> 

 

The fourth day of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 in Goa is witnessing a diverse celebration of cinema, For the prestigious ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal ten Indian and international feature films are in fray.

 

“Turkish filmmakers Elif Ada and Faysal Soysal, whose films are competing for the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal, interacted with the media at IFFI. Masterclasses explored Goa’s potential as a film hub, the importance of preserving its identity, and drawing inspiration from local culture to create original superhero stories. Filmmakers Rajendra Talak, Vijay Krishna Acharya, Ayan Mukerji and Basil Joseph participated. IFFI is also promoting inclusive cinema through accessibility partner Svayam. The festival continues to bring diverse cinematic voices, learning and collaboration onto one platform. Mahesh Chopade , Akashvani News, Panaji.” 

 

<><><> 

 

At the ongoing India International Trade Fair, the Hall of Inspiration is emerging as a major attraction for visitors. The pavilion, organised by Startup India, features around 600 Indian startups showcasing their advanced technologies, creative ideas and innovative solutions across various sectors. These include startups working in agritech, food products and other areas of innovation.

 

An exhibitor from Hansa AI, Shalendra, told Akashvani News that his organisation works on civic technology in collaboration with the government. He also highlighted two major projects, Scheme Connect and Hamara Neta App.

 

<><><> 

 

Benchmark domestic equity indices shed nearly 1.8 per cent today as Dalal Street witnessed intense selling pressure.

 

The Sensex plummeted 1 thousand 484 points to close at 82 thousand 436. The Nifty tumbled 451 points to settle at 25 thousand 350. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index tanked one per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index lost nearly 0.7 per cent. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 24 paise to close at 92 rupees and 91 paise against the US dollar. With Intekhab’s report Reshma Tiwari for Akashvani News”

 

<><><> 

 

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow. The Met Department has also forecast dense fog over East Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura during the next two days.

 

<><><> 

 

In Mens cricket, first test between New Zealand and India ended in a draw. In reply to India’s 720 for 9 in first innings, New Zealand made 239 for 5 in their second innings.

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi launches several development projects worth around 34 thousand 470 crore rupees in Vaishali district of Bihar; Reiterates commitment to build a Bihar that is stronger, more prosperous and full of opportunities.
  2. Prime Minister highlights hard work and achievements of India’s skilled youth at the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today inaugurated and dedicated to the nation several development projects worth around 34 thousand 470 crore rupees in Vaishali district of Bihar. Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister highlighted Bihar’s development journey, good governance and various welfare initiatives. Mr. Modi said, they are building a Bihar that is stronger, more prosperous and full of opportunities.

 

“The Prime Minister Narendra Modi was accorded a traditional welcome with a stole adorned with Bajjika artwork, flowers made of makhana, a garland of Aparajita flowers and bananas.

 

Following the welcome, the Prime Minister dedicated the six-lane Nitish Setu, built across the River Ganga, to the people of Bihar. Stretching approximately 20 kilometres, the bridge connects Kachchi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali district. With the inauguration of this bridge, traffic pressure on the Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu is expected to ease, while connectivity between North and South Bihar will become smoother.

 

Describing Nitish Setu as more than just a means of transportation, the Prime Minister said that the project would make people’s daily lives easier. He added that it would help local products reach larger markets and improve access to education and healthcare services.

 

In his address, the Prime Minister invoked the blessings of Chhathi Maiya and said that Bihar was celebrating a festival of development. He recalled that three decades ago, the people of Bihar had chosen the path of hope and faith, and that under the leadership of Nitish Kumar, the state had gained renewed confidence in good governance.

 

During the programme, the Prime Minister presented a total of 227 development projects to the state. These include the second 660-megawatt unit of the Buxar Thermal Power Project, along with several initiatives related to road construction, power distribution and transmission, irrigation, education, healthcare and urban development.

 

The Prime Minister also flagged off 100 electric buses under the PM-e-Bus initiative and participated in the Griha Pravesh ceremony for more than 26 thousand 900 beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban.

 

These projects are expected to strengthen connectivity, expand energy and urban infrastructure, improve public services and give fresh momentum to Bihar’s economic development. Nidhi Shree for Akashvani News, Patna.”

<><><> 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that skill development and technical training are key to empowering the youth and driving the country’s progress. Addressing the ‘5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh’ in Lucknow, he highlighted hard work and achievements of India’s skilled youth. Mr. Modi said that whether it is an IIT or an ITI, for him both are the nation’s invaluable assets and they represent the strength of our country and are the foundation of India’s future. He said that the skills and expertise students have acquired while studying at ITI are now a major source of strength for Viksit Bharat. The Prime Minister said that AI cannot take away the jobs of people who possess the right skills.

 

Fifty-two national-level toppers from Industrial Training Institutes and other skill-training institutions were felicitated at the event for their achievements. Speaking on the occasion, CM Yogi Adiyanath said that Prime Minister Modi launched the Skill India Mission in 2015, which has since been implemented at a rapid pace in Uttar Pradesh.

 

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said that Indian traditions have taught us that knowledge gives a person understanding, while skills provide the ability to perform. Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Jayant Chaudhary also graced the event.

 

Earlier in the day, addressing the platinum jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur, Prime Minister Modi called upon the youth to break the barriers of limited thinking and unlock the new possibilities. Mr. Modi said that limiting beliefs not only restrict the dreams and talent but also restricts the capabilities of the nation. Referring to a recent World Bank Report, the Prime Minister said that around 50 crore people in India have come out of poverty over the past 12 to 13 years.

<><><> 

Union Home Minister Amit Shah today described the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) as crucial to Arunachal Pradesh’s development and India’s energy security, while assuring the people of the Siang region that their cultural identity, traditional rights and interests would be protected. Addressing a gathering after conferring the President’s Police Colour on the Arunachal Pradesh Police at Banderdewa, Mr. Shah said the Centre would engage with affected communities through constructive dialogue to address their concerns and build trust. He also promised an attractive rehabilitation and resettlement package for project-affected families, asserting that development would not come at the cost of indigenous identity and rights.

<><><> 

The National Institute of Social Defence (NISD) has signed 23 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with universities and institutions in the presence of the Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment,  Dr Virendra Kumar in New Delhi today. Addressing the gathering, Dr Kumar said that the initiative would strengthen efforts towards enabling vulnerable individuals to lead dignified, self-reliant lives and contribute meaningfully to society.

<><><> 

External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar today held talks with the  Bulgarian Foreign Affairs Minister Velislava Petrova-Chamova in New Delhi. In his opening remarks, Dr Jaishankar said that India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) is expected to enter into force soon which will certainly provide new dynamism to the relationship. He said, in areas such as trade, technology and talent, India looks forward to doing much more with Europe. Dr Jaishankar said, India and the European Union have also signed a Security and Defence Partnership and a framework on mobility. He said, the visit of Bulgarian Foreign Affairs Minister has provided  an opportunity to assess the progress in bilateral ties and explore new areas of cooperation.

 

<><><> 

Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that historical connections have played a significant role in bringing Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) countries closer to one another. Addressing the joint sessions on the second day of the first SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi today, he said civilisations are not merely legacies of the past but living traditions whose knowledge continues to illuminate the present and inspire future generations.

<><><> 

The United Nations has expressed deep concern over the escalating hostilities in and around Yemen. Deputy Spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General, Farhan Haq, urged all parties to uphold their obligations under international humanitarian law, particularly the prohibition against targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure. He also called on all parties to take constant care to protect the civilian population and civilian objects from the effects of hostilities. Haq stressed that there is ultimately no military solution to the conflict, emphasizing the need for all parties to find a pathway back to political negotiations.

 

Meanwhile, in Yemen at least 41 people were killed in airstrikes attributed to Saudi Arabia over the past 24 hours. Citing health authorities in the Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa, Houthi-run Media reported that 28 people were injured in the attacks. Houthi military spokesperson said in a statement that the group targeted the Al-Shuqaiq power plant and Jazan port in Saudi Arabia’s Jazan region.

 <><><>

The much awaited Indian Panorama 2026 was formally inaugurated at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today, with Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Chanchal Kumar, declaring the showcase open. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Kumar highlighted the remarkable diversity of Indian cinema since its inception. Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker highlighted that the festival received 762 feature film entries and 358 non-feature film entries, taking the total to 1,120 submissions across 18 languages.

 

“In One of the key highlights of the day Indian Panorama Feature Film Jury chairman Madhur Bhandarkar said strong concepts, original storytelling and emotional appeal were the key considerations in selecting films for this year’s festival. The sixth edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow was also inaugurated at Kala Academy in Goa. Addressing the participants, Secretary in the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Chanchal Kumar, encouraged young filmmakers to draw inspiration from their cultural roots while allowing their imagination to reach global audiences. The festival also provided a platform for aspiring screenwriters through Prasar Bharati’s initiative, Page Se Pitch Tak. In Masterclass today in IFFI Girish Kasaravalli elaborated upon the The Moral Universe of Parallel Cinema: He expressed that even entertainment is also political. With 7 more days to go, IFFI is going to be a feast for cinelovers. MAHESH CHOPADE, AKASHVANI NEWS, PANAJI.”

<><><> 

In Badminton, India’s Lakshya Sen’s 13-match winning streak came to an end after he suffered a straight games defeat to Denmark’s World No. 3 Anders Antonsen in the men’s singles semifinal of the Hong Kong Open today. World No. 11 Sen went down 13-21, 13-21 against the Danish shuttler.

<><><> 

In Hockey, India defeated South Korea 2-1 in their second league stage match of Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal this evening.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has emphasised that cultural connections are the strongest guarantee of global peace. Inaugurating the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila in New Delhi today, the Prime Minister said, in 25 years since its inception the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) has significantly expanded cooperation in the areas of security, economy and connectivity. He said, in this context, cultural and civilizational cooperation will further strengthen relations among member countries.

 

 

The Prime Minister noted that 21st-century technology has created new possibilities for cultural connectivity. He highlighted that digital platforms have made knowledge sharing, cultural exchange and international collaboration easier than ever before and SCO countries should take full advantage of these new possibilities.

 

 

Prime Minister Modi also also undertook a walkthrough of the  exhibitions showcasing India’s archaeological, artistic and literary heritage titled “ASTITVA – The Essence of Our Existence. It offers an immersive account of Delhi’s history through archaeological evidence dating from 1200 BCE to 1200 CE.  The “Mahabharat Scroll Pavilion – Anant: A Rare 18th Century Mahabharata Scroll” will showcase an illustrated scroll reflecting India’s rich epic and artistic traditions.

Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shivraj Singh Chouhan today dedicated to the nation India’s first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine, developed by ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal. Describing

The Government has sanctioned one lakh 75 thousand additional houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban 2.0, with in-principle approval for another one lakh 50 thousand houses. Uttar Pradesh received approval for over one lakh houses, Maharashtra 19 thousand and Tamil Nadu 14 thousand. With these approvals, the total number of houses sanctioned under the scheme has crossed 24 lakh. States and Union Territories have been directed to ensure timely fund utilisation, release of assistance to beneficiaries and faster verification of pending applications.

Cyclone Akvan, which crossed the south Odisha and North Andhra coast this morning, has weakened into a deep depression while moving inland. The IMD has forecast further rainfall in northern Odisha tomorrow, even as the state government maintains a close watch on rivers and reservoirs. More from our Correspondent:

 

 

 

“Cyclone Akvan crossed the south Odisha coast near Gopalpur this morning with wind speeds of 70 to 80 kilometres per hour, gusting to 90 kilometres per hour. Standing paddy crops have been flattened in several coastal areas, while waterlogging has affected agricultural fields. Schools and Anganwadi centres will remain closed in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, Bhadrak and Kandhamal districts. Officials have confirmed that all dam gates are presently closed, with no water being discharged from reservoirs. The situation at Baghua dam is also being monitored. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News Bhuvneshwar.”

 

In Andhra Pradesh, rainfall has been reported mainly in Srikakulam district, while officials continue to monitor conditions. A report:

 

 

 

“In Andhra Pradesh, rainfall was reported mainly in Srikakulam district. There is no consolidated official report of casualties or major damage in the state so far. The cyclone is expected to weaken further as it moves inland. Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan over Bay of Bengal is moving north-northwestwards. It is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, passing close to the east of Gopalpur, by tomorrow noon. The India Meteorological Department said the cyclone has been moving at a speed of 13 kilometres per hour over the past six hours. Wind speeds at the time of landfall are expected to reach 90 to 100 kilometres per hour, with gusts of up to 110 kilometres per hour. Odisha and Andhra Pradesh governments have stepped up their preparedness to deal with the impending cyclone. In Odisha, more than one lakh five thousand people have already been evacuated to safer locations. Our correspondent has the details

 

 

 

“As a precautionary measure, the state government has already started the evacuation process in view of the impending cyclone. The government has set up over nine thousand shelters and deployed over 3 hundred emergency response teams, including NDRF and ODRAF, across vulnerable places in several districts. As of now, over 1 lakh 5 thousand people have been evacuated and shifted to safer places. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said the government is making all necessary preparations, with priority being given to ensure “zero casualties”. The Puri Shree Jagannath Temple Administration urged devotees to plan their visits in line with weather advisories in view of the Cyclonic storm. In view of Cyclone Akvan, Indian Railways has cancelled and rescheduled train services. With SN Patnaik this is Smrutirekha for Akashvani News Cuttack.”

 

 

 

The Andhra Pradesh Government has also intensified its preparations to tackle the approaching cyclone. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

“Heavy rainfall is likely in parts of Srikakulam district. Moderate rain may occur in Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Polavaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli and Kakinada districts. Strong winds may uproot trees and damage temporary structures. Low-lying areas may also face waterlogging. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has advised fishermen not to venture into the sea. People living along the North Andhra coast have been asked to remain alert. Farmers have been advised to protect harvested paddy from rain and follow official advisories. Allu Murali Akashvani News,Vijaywada.”

 

 

 

Under the influence of Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan, several districts of West Bengal are also experiencing rainfall.

The Government has revised the validity period of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates for different categories of vehicles. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, in this regard. According to a Gazette notification, the validity of PUC certificates will now depend on the vehicle’s emission standards, category and age.

 

 

“Under the amended rules, vehicles complying with BS-I, BS-II and BS-III emission norms will have a PUC certificate valid for three months, while vehicles complying with BS-IV norms will have a validity of six months. For non-transport vehicles complying with BS-VI emission norms, the certificate will be valid for three years for vehicles up to six years old. While for vehicles more than six years and up to ten years old, the validity will be for one year. For vehicles older than ten years, the validity will be six months. In the case of transport vehicles complying with BS-VI norms, the certificate validity for vehicles up to six years old will be for two years. The validity of the certificate will be one year for vehicles of more than six years and up to ten years old, and six months for vehicles older than ten years. Akshit Vaidyan for Akashvani News, Delhi”

The stage is all set for the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, which is set to begin in Goa from the 20th of this month. The nine-day festival will bring together filmmakers, artists and cinema enthusiasts from across the world, celebrating the diversity of global cinema. Among the highlights this year is a dedicated new Animation segment, celebrating the artistry and emotional depth of animated storytelling. More from our Correspondent:

 

 

 

“Animation has the unique ability to bring drawings to life and tell stories that connect with audiences across cultures and generations. Adding a new dimension to this year’s festival, the 57th International Film Festival of India has introduced a dedicated Animation segment featuring five international animated feature films from Japan, France, China, Singapore and the United States. The selection includes Cherry and Virgin from Japan, Jim Queen from France, Light Pillar from China, Magic Atlas from Singapore and Ray Gunn from the United States. The films explore a range of themes, including love, identity, loneliness, memory and resistance. Through this new segment, IFFI aims to showcase the creative possibilities of animation and bring diverse international stories to festival audiences. With Vishnu and Alex, this is Saira Mujtaba, from Panaji, Goa.”

Leaders of Quad countries met in Manila today on the sidelines of ASEAN Summit. At the meeting, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, Manila and Quad have shared an age-old and special bond. He said cooperation among the four countries covered a wide range of areas, including maritime security, trusted supply chains, emerging technologies and disaster response. The Prime Minister said, holding a Quad meeting once again in the historic city of Manila, marks an important milestone. He called for setting concrete goals to strengthen cooperation among the four member countries in the next phase.

 

 

 

During the meeting, US President Donald Trump highlighted tha Quad’s revival and added that their cooperation has grown. He said, these countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable and most prosperous Indo-Pacific. Mr. Trump said, they have outstanding relationships and coordinate closely on matters of regional security and economic diplomacy. Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi and Australian PM Anthony Albanese were also present in the meeting.

 

 

The leaders opposed unilateral attempts to change the status quo through force or coercion and expressed concern over economic coercion, including arbitrary export restrictions.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Earlier today, Prime Minister Modi addressed the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit in Manila. He highlighted the growing partnership between India and ASEAN and called for greater cooperation to ensure peace, stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific region. The Prime Minister congratulated Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on his successful chairship of ASEAN. Mr Modi said, India’s Act East policy had given India-ASEAN relations a new momentum and depth over the past several years.

                        

 

Highlighting the expansion of bilateral cooperation, PM Modi said the partnership, built on shared culture and heritage, was now expanding into new areas such as digital technologies, defence and space.

 

 

Referring to the global situation, PM Modi observed that the world had faced one crisis after another over the past few years. He said the summit’s theme, “Navigating Our Future Together,” held particular significance in the current global context. He added that India and ASEAN possessed the capabilities and shared resolve to make the region a symbol of peace and stability. India and ASEAN agreed to deepen cooperation on disaster management and early warning systems.

 

 

 

Expressing confidence in the outcome of the summit, he said the meeting would elevate the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to new heights and contribute to building a secure, inclusive and prosperous Indo-Pacific.

 

 

 

Later, Prime Minister Modi attended the 21st East Asia Summit in Manila. PM Modi called for stronger regional cooperation and emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in addressing key regional and international challenges. He also rolled out rolls out seafarers’ safety initiative to bolster maritime security at East Asia Summit.

 

 

 

The summit brought together leaders of ASEAN member states and their eight dialogue partners to discuss regional and international issues.

 

 

 Our correspondent covering the Summit has more on the outcomes of ASEAN- India Summit and East Asia Summit.

 

 

 

“Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Manila, resulted in several important outcomes aimed at strengthening India’s engagement with ASEAN and East Asian countries.

 

 

 

During the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit, India proposed a long-term maritime cooperation plan, joint cyber forensics training, nuclear energy technical exchanges and an ASEAN-India Space Hackathon.

 

 

 

Other initiatives include cooperation in critical minerals, youth exchanges, enhanced scholarships at Nalanda University, a Creative Partnership Pavilion at WAVES 2027 and free e-visas for ASEAN tourists visiting India.

 

 

 

At the 21st East Asia Summit, India proposed a Seafarers’ Safety Initiative, an East Asia Summit Cyber Crime Conference at the National Forensic Science University, a Maritime Heritage Festival at Lothal and a University Conclave at Nalanda to promote academic cooperation.

 

 

 

The visit also saw the adoption of three important documents including the ASEAN-India Joint Statement on Cooperation in Disaster Management, the East Asia Summit Leaders’ Statement on Strengthening Cooperation Against Online Scams and Related Offences. With Ishfaq Shah’s report from Manila, tripti srivastava, AKASHVANI NEWS.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today held a series of bilateral meetings with leaders of the Philippines, Thailand and Singapore on the sidelines of the ASEAN-India Summit and East Asia Summit.

 

 

Prime Minister Modi and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in defence, security, trade and investment. The Ministry of External Affairs said, the two leaders reviewed their Strategic Partnership and welcomed the growing cooperation in Defence, Space, Railway infrastructure, Financial Technology and Trade.

 

 

The two leaders exchanged views on key regional and global developments and reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral ties. The Ministry said, defence cooperation remains an important pillar of the partnership, with India supplying BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles to the Philippines in 2024.

India’s electronic goods exports registered strong growth of 44 per cent during April-September this year increasing from over 22 billion dollars in the corresponding period of 2025-26 to around 32 billion dollars. While smartphones continued to account for the largest share of the electronics export basket, non-smartphone electronics recorded significantly faster growth, reflecting the broadening and diversification of India’s electronics exports across components, printed circuit boards, communication equipment, memory products and storage devices.

 

 

 

Exports of smartphones increased by over 35 per cent, from 13 billion dollars in April-September last year to over 18 billion dollars during April-September this year.

 

 

Non-smartphone electronics exports recorded a growth of over 56 per cent.

The draft electoral roll under the Special Summary Revision 2027 published in Uttar Pradesh today, with claims and objections to be accepted from November 17 to December 16.

 

 

According to the list state’s electorate has increased by around 18.84 lakh since the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

 

 

As per the draft electoral roll for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, the state’s total number of electorate is 13 crore 58 lakh 68 thousand and 905.

 

 

Chief Electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa said that the claims and objections can be filed from today to 16th next month. The disposal of claims and objections is scheduled to be completed by December 28, with the final electoral roll set to be published on January 4, 2027.

The Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” prevailing over South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal has moved slowly northwards at a slow pace of three kilometer per hour during the past 6 hours. It is moving closer to the coastal states of Tamilnadu, Andhra and Odisha and is likely to intensify further in the coming days. The India Meteorological Department has warned of heavy to very heavy rainfall and strong winds along the coastal areas. More from our Andhra Pradesh correspondent –

 

 

“Cyclonic Storm Akvan over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify further and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. The India Meteorological Department says the storm is expected to become a Severe Cyclonic Storm tonight and a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm by Thursday morning.

 

 

 

It is expected to continue moving towards the northwest and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on Friday, as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm. Wind speeds may reach 120 to 130 kilometres per hour, with gusts up to 145 kilometres per hour.

 

 

 

The IMD has forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh tomorrow. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at several places on Thursday and Friday, with extremely heavy rainfall possible at isolated places.

 

 

 

Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the affected areas for the next four days. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

 

 

 

Our Chennai Correspondent has filed this report:

 

 

 

“The cyclone is very likely to move slowly and intensify further into a Severe Cyclonic Storm tonight . The cyclone is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm around 19th November morning and continue  moving northwestward,.  Akvan will then turn into a severe cyclonic storm and  cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, around noon of 20th with wind speed gusting upto 145 kmph. According to the weather department,  moderate to heavy rains are likely over  isolated places in  Northern Tamilnadu in the coming days.

The Commission for Air Quality Management Sub-Committee has revoked GRAP Stage III in Delhi in view of a downward trend, with the air quality index reaching 204 today. The CAQM however, said that all actions under GRAP Stages I and II and restrictions as per order passed 30th of last month shall remain in force. The restriction includes restriction of outdoor construction works across Delhi NCR. It has given exemption to construction works related to state duties and national interest. The circular also directs State Government and private offices to operate with up to 50 percent of the staff strength attending physically.
